headshot.altText: Official headshot of Rep. Jake Auchincloss
headshot.usageNote: Use as the primary profile reference image until replaced by a campaign-approved or official congressional press image.

bio.oneLine: Jake Auchincloss is a Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 4th Congressional District.
bio.short: Jake Auchincloss represents Massachusetts's 4th Congressional District in the U.S. House.  A Marine veteran and former Newton city councilor, he works on issues including transportation, housing, health care, foreign policy, China competitiveness, and technology policy.
bio.standard: Jake Auchincloss is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 4th Congressional District.  Born in Newton, Massachusetts, he served as a Marine officer, including service in Afghanistan, before earning an M.B.A. and entering local government on the Newton City Council.  In Congress, Auchincloss has focused on transportation, housing, health care, pharmacy benefit manager reform, foreign policy, China competitiveness, and technology policy.  His committee and caucus work includes Energy and Commerce, Transportation and Infrastructure, and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.
bio.long: Jake Auchincloss is a Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 4th Congressional District.  Born in Newton, Massachusetts, he studied government and economics at Harvard before serving as a Marine officer, including service in Afghanistan.  After returning to civilian life, he earned an M.B.A. and won a seat on the Newton City Council.  Auchincloss later ran for Congress in 2020 after Rep. Joseph P. Kennedy III left the seat to run for the U.S. Senate.  In Congress, he has built a profile around transportation, housing, health care, pharmacy benefit manager reform, technology policy, foreign policy, Afghanistan, China competitiveness, and support for U.S. allies.  His current profile includes work with the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.
